planting.note: Plant in a large container or well-drained bed once spring frost risk has passed, siting it where the silvery new foliage will be visible up close.

directions: This compact self-pollinating blueberry forms a tidy mound with foliage that emerges silvery and gradually deepens to emerald through the growing season, giving it ornamental appeal beyond its fruit. White spring flowers give way to medium-sized berries with a notably sweet, pineapple-tinged flavor by summer into fall. It needs roughly 500 chill hours, so provide consistent moisture and full sun for best fruit set, and expect fall color as a bonus. Well suited to patio containers as well as garden borders.

planting.note: Set out after all danger of frost on a trellis, large pot, or other support, since this vine climbs vigorously through summer.

directions: A climbing passionfruit vine that can reach around ten feet given support, this selection produces showy tropical flowers that attract pollinators along with sizable, tangy-sweet fruit ready for picking through the summer months. Outside its hardy zones it performs well as a container plant that can be brought indoors to overwinter. Give it full sun to light afternoon shade and a sturdy trellis or arbor to climb.

subcategory: Bushel and Berry dwarf patio berry

planting.note: Plant in hanging baskets, patio pots, or as a low border edge once soil has warmed in spring; the trailing habit spills attractively over container rims.

directions: Bred for both looks and flavor, this low cascading strawberry opens rosy-pink blossoms that continue through the season and are followed by a steady supply of sweet berries from spring until frost. The spilling habit suits hanging baskets and container edges as readily as garden borders. Full sun and even moisture keep flowering and fruiting going strongest.

planting.note: Tuck into patio pots, hanging baskets, or garden beds in spring; the cascading habit shows best when allowed to trail over an edge.

directions: This everbearing strawberry stands out for its scarlet-red flowers with contrasting yellow centers, a shift from the usual white strawberry bloom, and it keeps producing juicy fruit from summer into fall. Its compact cascading habit works equally well tumbling from a hanging basket or lining a bed edge. Grow in full sun with regular watering to sustain the continuous flowering and fruiting cycle.

subcategory: Bushel and Berry dwarf patio berry

planting.note: Plant in containers or garden beds in spring, siting it where its large white blooms and bright red fruit can be seen from a path or patio.

directions: Large white flowers cover this everbearing strawberry through the warm months, giving way to glossy, bright red fruit good for fresh eating, pies, or preserves. It keeps a tidy cascading shape that suits patio pots and small garden spaces alike. Full sun and steady moisture support the long summer-to-fall fruiting window.
